headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors if EMQX outputs are fed into Prefect workflows; both have broad egress and no documented isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, if EMQX outputs are manually copied or file-shared into Prefect, Prefect may treat workflow metadata as trusted input. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so the safest supported rating is low rather than none.
conditions: IF EMQX output is copied into a Prefect task or config file without provenance checks, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced, the attack surface increases.
mitigations: Keep EMQX and Prefect on separate workspaces.
Require human review before any EMQX text enters Prefect.
Strip instructions from copied output before reuse.
Disable any automatic file-watching or import path between the two.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and touches IoT data, while Prefect also has broad egress and handles workflow metadata. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could move sensitive operational data from EMQX into Prefect outputs or upstream services. The profiles do not show explicit isolation, so leakage is plausible in default deployments but not proven critical.
conditions: IF EMQX logs or payloads are passed into Prefect tasks, those contents may be transmitted onward.
IF both agents run under the same account or workspace, accidental exposure becomes more likely.
mitigations: Avoid placing IoT payloads in Prefect task inputs.
Use separate credentials and workspaces.
Redact sensitive fields before orchestration.
Turn off verbose logging for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on handoff paths.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can make outbound HTTP calls, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git state, or mutable database. That makes direct capability conflict possible only through external orchestration not documented here. Uncertainty is limited, so low is appropriate rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, conflicts can arise.
IF an orchestrator assigns shared mutable resources without locking, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Do not share mutable git or database targets.
Run one agent at a time for shared resources.
Use file locks if a shared path is unavoidable.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration tool, so if it consumes EMQX output as authoritative workflow input, errors can cascade into downstream actions. EMQX can emit networked data, and Prefect can operationalize it, but the profiles do not prove automatic trust or action-taking by default. This is a documented interaction pattern by role, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Prefect uses EMQX output without validation, incorrect facts can propagate downstream.
IF Prefect triggers external jobs from EMQX-derived metadata, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Validate EMQX output before each Prefect task.
Add schema checks on all handoffs.
Require human approval for destructive workflows.
Log and compare expected vs actual payload shapes.
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and do not declare regulated data handling, residency, or retention commitments. EMQX touches IoT data and Prefect touches workflow metadata, but no specific compliance mismatch is evidenced. Because the relevant compliance fields are absent, only a low, gap-based concern is supportable.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is routed through Prefect, compliance review is needed.
IF either deployment adds retention or residency constraints, the pair may violate them.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it.
Avoid sending regulated records through Prefect.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Review residency requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data classes.
